title: Fix coons_cage technique prompt (cube.mesh transition and boolean_math port example)
description: The Coons Patch Control Cage technique prompt shipped to the voyage agent has two prose-level inaccuracies that burn rounds on real runs. (1) The pipeline diagram 'cube → loop_cuts → assign_bezier_handles → ...' implies a single .geometry chain, but cube only exposes .mesh — the MESH→GEOMETRY_BUNDLE handoff happens inside loop_cut (which accepts both). First-time authors hit 'Node base has no output port geometry. Valid outputs: mesh'. Fix: one sentence clarifying 'cube outputs only .mesh — feed into loop_cut(mesh=...), then use .geometry downstream'. (2) The selection section says 'Combine with boolean_math(AND/OR) as needed' without showing port names. Authors extrapolate from float_math(operation=ADD) and write boolean_math(operation=OR).result, which errors; real ports are mode= and .value. Fix: replace the prose hint with a tiny example showing 'sel = boolean_math(mode=OR, a=x.selection, b=y.selection)' and threading sel.value into the next op. Surfaced from a live skull voyage run; see VOYAGE-46 for the broader tool-schema lookup fix that would also catch these drifts automatically. Note: VOYAGE-46 (tool-schema lookup) is the structural fix; this ticket is the immediate prose patch.
definition-of-done: 1. Technique prompt file (likely under Daud/src/daud/voyage/ or similar) updated with the cube.mesh clarification. 2. boolean_math prose hint replaced with a working code example using mode= and .value. 3. Any other *_math example in the prompt uses the correct per-node input/output port names. 4. Ideally, these examples are lint-checked against the live tool / node schemas in CI so the prose cannot silently drift again.
testing-plan: 1. Run voyage-batch on Skull.obj with the updated prompt; verify the agent's first validate_dsl call succeeds without the cube.geometry or boolean_math.operation errors that occurred in the baseline run. 2. grep the prompt for any remaining boolean_math(operation= or .result references. 3. CI lint (if added) catches a synthetic bad example added to the prompt.
